To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) in a half diallels of five homozygous inbreds for a single recessive self-incompatibility allele there was significant genetic variation for seed production on self-pollinated and outcross-pollinated inflorences; (b) on outcross-pollination the additive genetic variation for seed set per flower site was significant and the simple additive dominance model explained the variation well; and (c) on self-pollination, additive genetic variation was not present

The self seed set of a progeny from a half diall between five inbred lines homozygous at the S-locus was determined to be a complex character, controlled by both additive and non-additive gene action.

In the progenies of the half-diallel of five inbred lines homozygous recessive for the same S-allele, significant genetic variation was found for outcross seed production and its two components; additive gene action was present for outcross but absent for self seed production; and complex gene interactions were responsible for the variation observed on self-pollinated progenies.
